learner_visual_status.note: Manual photo-led card enrichment with one pixel-reviewed exact-source original image, 4-taxon genus comparison, diagnostic photo checklist. Unshown anatomy and nativity hold preserved.

best_field_traits: Perennial; unlike many rosette-grasses it may lack an obvious winter basal rosette.
Largest stem blades commonly 6–12 cm long and roughly 7–15 mm wide; often cordate at the base, but not consistently.
Sheath backs often hairless or sparsely hairy; marginal and collar hairs may still be conspicuous.
True ligule a minute fringe or absent; inspect at magnification.
Open, rather few-spikeleted spring panicles; spikelets broadly about 2.1–3.2 mm long.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Stem blade base carefully flattened showing true cordate versus tapering attachment with 1-mm scale
Blade/sheath collar clearly spread showing minute or absent true ligule independently from margin cilia
One intact spring flowering panicle and same rooted shoot
Three mature 2.1–3.2 mm spikelets with calibrated mm ruler, glume details; existing flowering parts already covered

confused_with: other Dichanthelium species (not yet represented in this learner)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Against tiny-spikeleted D. lindheimeri (~1.3–1.6 mm) check actual size and hair ligule; against D. oligosanthes (~2.9–4 mm) compare broad sometimes cordate stem leaf base and very short/absent true ligule; against D. pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm) compare broader stem leaves vs narrow blades and extremely short 0.25–0.5 mm collar fringe. All photos source-determined, not Hays vouchers.
comparisons.photo_context: Four real already archived source-labelled images are incorporated into a genus comparison. The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.
not_reliable_alone: Airy panicle silhouette in a single season
Habitat or presumed annual/perennial condition from clipped stem
Ligule hair lengths or spikelet sizes inferred from photos without rulers
The older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri name interpreted as a new separate species

Four physical original JPGs reused with creators/individual licenses including BY-NC/SA. A true ligule, blade base and glume-macro still needed; no new media bytes.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Rosette panicgrass — see photo evidence, then check the plant
steps: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Panicles often overlap. Show spring/autumn phase, true leaf collar, and at least three mature measured spikelets from the same plant before a firm species call.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The literature-size figures and diagnostic leaf features are not verified by the stored photos. Do not attach falsely precise or microscopic arrows.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Broad, often heart-based stem leaves + small open panicle; confirm the collar and spikelet
field_id_short_tiles.details: On an attached perennial shoot find relatively broad lanceolate stem blades, commonly 7–15 mm wide in the WFO regional treatment (Go Botany lists 5–10 mm), sometimes cordate/clasping at the base. Follow the same culm to an open, relatively few-spikeleted spring panicle (about 5–10 cm in the WFO treatment). The eight stored source-identified photos show live leafy shoots, open panicles and flowering spikelets, but do NOT establish a rooted voucher, exact blade-base shape, true inner ligule or species by themselves.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD-READY COMBINED CUE — SOURCE-IDENTIFIED, NOT MEASURED SAME-PLANT PROOF

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · FOLLOW THE GROWTH FORM
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial branching grass; spring and late-season shoots can differ
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace an entire attached shoot and record its root crown, spring primary flowering panicle and later-season leafy secondary branches if available. The source describes a perennial with branching stems, and many Dichanthelium have seasonally different flowering phases. Do not assert that a dense winter rosette is always visible in D. commutatum: treatments differ on basal-rosette expression. Current woodland-habit photo shows shoots meeting litter, NOT an exposed connected perennial crown.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — CONNECTED CROWN AND SEASONAL SHOOTS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE TRUE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: True ligule minute, often about 0–0.5 mm; do not measure sheath-edge hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: Peel the blade away from its sheath and inspect the INNER blade–sheath junction under 10–20× with a millimeter scale. The USGS Louisiana key gives a ~0.5-mm ligule; Go Botany gives up to 0.5 mm; WFO notes a minute hair fringe or absence, depending on treatment. Distinguish the actual ligule from long marginal/sheath hairs. Existing Alex Abair collar images show OUTER hairs and leaf junction only, not a measured free inner ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — TRUE INNER LIGULE AT 0.1–1 MM SCALE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Typically ~2.1–3.2 mm long; photograph three with a real scale
field_id_short_tiles.details: Measure at least three mature, source-vouchered oval spikelets from the SAME rooted flowering plant against a 1-mm scale at 10–20×. WFO gives ~2.1–3.2 mm; Go Botany ~2.2–3.2 mm. Panicle macro panels show real oval spikelets and fine pedicels, but their images have no calibration. Flower colors, hairiness and panicle openness cannot substitute for mature measurements.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · SEPARATE GLUMES AND LEMMAS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Short lower glume; upper glume + lower sterile lemma; upper fertile lemma awnless
field_id_short_tiles.details: Under a dissecting lens separate the FIRST/LOWER glume (WFO usually about one-third or a little more of the 2.1–3.2-mm spikelet; Nicaragua treatment ~0.5–1.5 mm), upper glume, lower sterile-floret lemma and firm upper fertile lemma/palea. The fertile lemma has NO awn (Go Botany: 0 mm), so never label a visible flower filament, purple anther or red stigma as an awn. A partly opened existing source photograph exposes pale surfaces, but individual glume/lemma boundaries and veins have NOT been independently resolved or measured.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — DISSECTED GLUMES, FERTILE LEMMA AND SCALE; NO ORGAN ARROWS YET

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Leaf base + true ligule + measured spikelets beat airy-head guesses
field_id_short_tiles.details: D. lindheimeri usually has much smaller ripe spikelets (~1.3–1.6 mm) and a conspicuous longer collar hair fringe. D. oligosanthes overlaps in broad foliage but usually has larger spikelets (~2.9–4 mm) and a longer hair fringe. D. pedicellatum has narrower spring blades (~1.3–5.5 mm) and a very short ~0.25–0.5-mm fringe; its ~3–3.5-mm spikelets overlap D. oligosanthes. These are literature comparisons, not calibrated in current look-alike panels. Record Dichanthelium sp. when the same-plant leaf base, true collar and mature spikelets cannot be reconciled.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD-READY LOOK-ALIKE KEY — SPECIES CONFIRMATION STILL REQUIRES CALIBRATED EVIDENCE
